cards.text: This is a psalm of David, king of Israel, and he skips the small talk with the LORD: "I call upon You, O LORD; come quickly to me. Hear my voice when I call to You." Not "whenever You get a minute, Lord." QUICKLY!

cards.question: David asks for his prayer to be set before the LORD like something from Israel's worship. What is it?

cards.text: David wants his uplifted hands to be like the evening offering. Me, I've got no hands, so when I praise, this mustache goes UP like a goalpost!
Then David turns the spotlight on himself and asks the LORD to set a guard. Not at the city gate, friend, somewhere WAY more personal.

cards.question: David asks the LORD to keep watch at the door of his lips. What does he want help with?

cards.text: Then David goes deeper than his mouth. He doesn't want to take part in works of wickedness with men who do iniquity.

cards.question: David asks the LORD not to let his ___ be drawn to any evil thing.
True or false: David asks to enjoy the delicacies of men who do iniquity, as long as he stays out of their works.

cards.text: No fancy delicacies from that crowd. Then David says something you don't hear every day: he's fine getting hit, as long as it's from the right person.

cards.question: Who is David willing to let strike him?
How does David see a rebuke from a righteous man?

answers.text: as a kind act of love
as a punishment he has earned
as a test of his pride

cards.text: He even calls it oil for his head and says he won't refuse it. Meanwhile a baker says my oven's running hot and I'm defensive for three whole seconds, until I check and it IS.

cards.question: True or false: David says his prayer is ever against the deeds of the wicked.

cards.text: David's still praying to the LORD. Now he looks ahead to a time when their rulers are thrown down from the cliffs.

cards.question: When those rulers are thrown down from the cliffs, what does David say the people will do?
True or false: David says the people will listen to his words because they are afraid of him.

cards.text: Then the psalm gets heavy. David says, "so our bones have been scattered at the mouth of Sheol."

cards.question: David compares those bones scattered at the mouth of Sheol to a picture from everyday life. What is it?

cards.text: And then David turns it all around with one little word: "But". Friend, I spent years in the back of a junk drawer waiting for a "but" that GOOD.

cards.question: Even with bones scattered at the mouth of Sheol, David says his eyes are fixed on ___.
True or false: David says he seeks refuge in his own strength.

cards.text: Then David asks God to keep him from the snares and lures the evildoers have laid for him. These folks didn't set one trap, they built a whole OBSTACLE COURSE!

cards.question: David asks for the wicked to fall into their own ___ while he passes by in ___.

findings.problem: The right answer 'incense' is the only answer without 'the', while both wrong answers start with 'the' ('the showbread', 'the firstfruits'). That makes the right answer look different from the others.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: In Psalm 141:4, David asks the LORD for something: 'Do not let my heart be drawn to any evil thing or take part in works of wickedness.' The card turns that request into a statement about what David wants ('He doesn't want to take part in works of wickedness'). It should keep it as a request to the LORD.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: The setup line 'as long as it's from the right person' rules out the wrong answer 'his enemies' on card 10 before the baker chooses. It also points toward 'righteous'.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: This is a 'who' question, but the wrong answers 'his enemies' and 'a foreign king' are generic descriptions. They should be real details from somewhere in the Bible.

rule.text: For who, which thing and where questions, wrong answers are real details from somewhere in the Bible, like Joppa when the right answer is Tarshish.

findings.problem: 'Says he won't refuse it' turns the BSB request 'let me not refuse it' (Psalm 141:5) into a statement or promise. It should stay a request.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: The question says 'those rulers', which points back to the story card before it. That card is no longer on screen. The question doesn't say whose rulers they are or give the context itself.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: The punchline 'waiting for a "but" that GOOD' sounds just like 'butt' when said aloud, so it reads as innuendo or crude humor.

rule.text: No cursing, crude humor, innuendo, or social or political commentary.
